thread.title: Apple earnings preview, chipmakers, and European market impact

author: uk.finance.yahoo.com
title: Apple earnings preview, chipmakers, and European market impact
text: People use their phones outside an Apple store in Beijing, China January 7, 2019. Photo: REUTERS/Thomas Peter/File Photo More Here are the top business, market, and economic stories you should be watching today in the UK, Europe, and abroad: All eyes on European chipmakers Shares in European-listed microchip suppliers were a mixed bag on Tuesday ahead of Apple ( AAPL ) reporting earnings later today. STMicroelectronics ( STM.PA ) was down by 0.6% and Austrian chipmaker AMS ( AMS.VI ) fell by 1.4% during early trading. Dialog Semiconductor ( DLG.DE ) was up 1.6% after it had already proven it weathered the Apple iPhone sales slump. BE Semiconductor ( BESI.AS ) was also up 1%. Earlier this month, Apple unexpectedly slashed its revenue forecast for the fiscal first quarter of 2019, citing weakness in its key market of China and lower-than-anticipated iPhone revenue. It said it expected $84bn for the period, which is about an 8% reduction from its previous estimates. As Yahoo Finance’s Emily McCormick pointed out, this had been Apple’s first negative pre-announcement since June 2002 . This was down to worse-than-anticipated iPhone upgrades as well as economic deceleration “particularly in Greater China,” according to Apple. China’s economic slowdown has become a great worry for Apple and related companies. For example, chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ) slashed its fiscal fourth-quarter 2019 revenue guidance by $500m due to “deteriorating macroeconomic conditions, particularly in China” while Intel ( INTC ) last week missed Wall Street’s expectations. Apple shares closed down by nearly 1%, in line with the Nasdaq which was off more than 1%. Meanwhile, Apple sent out a warning to iPhone users that it is fixing a bug that allows eavesdropping on their devices through the FaceTime app. READ MORE: Two things to watch for when Apple reports results Investors flee to safety stocks amid US-China trade fear Asian markets had a bumpy ride today, as hopes for a long-awaited US-China trade deal were dashed after the US doled out sweeping criminal charges against China’s telecom giant Huawei. Chinese shares closed up, even though they opened in the red, recovering in the afternoon. China’s blue-chip index rose by 0.4% and Japan’s Nikkei increased by 0.1%. However, MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was still down. European markets rose on Tuesday as investors avoided companies exposed to trade frictions, such l uxury goods, technology, and auto stocks. Pharmaceuticals were being supped up, such as Sartorius Stedim ( DIM.PA ) which jumped over 13%. Britain’s FTSE ( ^FTSE ), Germany’s DAX ( ^GDAXI ), and France’s CAC ( ^FCHI ) are all up, with the FTSE 100 leading the pack by over 1%. Potential Brexit delay boosts pound UK parliament will table amendments, with possible changes to the Irish ‘backstop’ element of the deal, and vote on prime minister Theresa May’s Brexit deal at 7pm local time. It is unclear how the political deadlock will pan out in Britain because her deal was previously voted down, by British MPs, and the EU said it will not renegotiate the agreement she arranged with member states. However there is a possibility that Brexit will be delayed as MPs may push to extend Article 50 — the notification that Britain will leave the European Union. With less than two months before the UK is meant to sever ties with the bloc, there is an impasse among UK politicians divided over the terms of the divorce. A Brexit delay would help give more time to seal a deal that will get through parliament. The pound’s movements have become a barometer of how investors are viewing Brexit talks, and how the UK economy is faring in light of the impending departure. The pound is rising on expectations of a delay. Source: Yahoo Finance
